title: SpliceAI nominates a deep intronic PKHD1 variant in a neonate who died of ARPKD; RNA validation confirms it and the parents proceed to IVF with PGT-M
summary: SpliceAI scored a deep intronic PKHD1 variant 0.98; RNA studies confirmed aberrant splicing; parents used the diagnosis for IVF with PGT-M.
account: A male infant was delivered at an outside hospital at 34+2 weeks and had bilateral kidney enlargement with innumerable tiny cysts consistent with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease; he was cared for in the Mount Sinai neonatal intensive care unit, New York, and died at two days of life. Whole-genome sequencing found a known paternal pathogenic missense variant, and SpliceAI scores in the NICUnet Rareservoir identified a maternally inherited deep intronic PKHD1 variant scoring 0.98, which RNA studies on maternal urine-derived renal epithelial cells confirmed creates a novel exon with a premature stop codon; GeneDx classified it likely pathogenic. After genetic counseling the parents proceeded with IVF and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders within one year of the death.
purpose: SpliceAI is a deep-learning model built to predict the effect of DNA variants on RNA splicing; nominating a splice-altering deep intronic variant is exactly its intended use.
developer: SpliceAI authors (Jaganathan et al., Cell 2019), as cited in the case report; the developing organization is not named in the text on file
deployer: NICUnet consortium / Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (Rareservoir variant database)
segment: Genome reanalysis in a neonatal research network
taxonomy_note: The patient had died, so the diagnosis changed the bereaved parents' reproductive planning rather than the infant's outcome.

ratings.reason: An identifiable family received a definitive molecular cause of their son's death and used it for IVF with preimplantation genetic testing to avoid recurrence of a lethal disease; life-changing for the family, not life-saving for the patient.

ai_role.statement: SpliceAI's score (0.98; among 78,575 rare intronic PKHD1 variants in gnomAD only one scored higher) nominated the maternally inherited deep intronic variant as the second allele. Pathogenicity was then established by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing of maternal urine-derived cells and by GeneDx's likely-pathogenic classification. The AI's contribution was candidate selection; without it the second allele would have remained unexplained. Authors declare no relevant financial interests.
